---
title: "R & GitHub Personal Reference Guide"
---

# Goal

The goal of this portfolio piece is to create a personal quick-reference guide for using R and Git/GitHub that I can rely on after graduation. Because I plan to continue working with data in research settings, I want a resource that documents core technical workflows while also reflecting my learning and growth throughout this course.

By organizing concepts, writing example code, and documenting common errors and their solutions, this guide helps reinforce the skills I am developing in Dr. Garrison’s Applied Data Psychology course. Writing this reference helps me to explain ideas clearly, which deepens my understanding and makes it easier to revisit material later.

This guide will include common challenges I have encountered in R and Git, explanations of why those issues occur, strategies for debugging them, and guidance on how to ask clear technical questions. I will also incude links to resources so I can quickly find help in the future.

This portfolio is intentionally iterative and expandable. I plan to continue refining and adding to it throughout the semester as my skills grow.


# 1. Setup & Environment Configuration
Configuring R, RStudio, and Git/GitHub, organizing project folders, and managing packages.

# 2. Data Import & Inspection
Reading data into R, understanding data structure, checking variable types, and exploring datasets.

# 3. Data Cleaning & Tidy Data
Handling missing values, renaming variables, reshaping data, and preparing datasets for analysis.

# 4. Data Transformation with dplyr
Filtering, selecting, mutating, grouping, and summarizing data using tidy workflows.

# 5. Data Visualization with ggplot2
Reusable plotting templates and strategies for creating clear and interpretable figures.

# 6. Working with Multiple Datasets & Text
Joining datasets, cleaning text variables, and managing categorical data.

# 7. Modeling & Statistical Integration
Fitting basic models, interpreting output, and integrating modeling into tidy workflows.

# 8. Writing Clean, Reusable Code
Writing functions, structuring scripts, avoiding repetition, and scaling analyses.

# 9. Debugging & Asking Good Questions
Common errors, troubleshooting strategies, and how to ask clear technical questions.

# 10. Git & GitHub Workflow
Version control basics, collaboration, and best practices for managing projects.
